reviews.reason: The route, auth bypass path, and sink all exist exactly as claimed; the finding remains UNCERTAIN because no mechanism in this plugin's source exposes the /.api_token file value to an unauthenticated remote attacker. The Phase 3a 'sink not found' issue was a line-matching artefact: store_token() is declared at ApiKeyManager.php:18 and the update_option() sink is on line 21, which is correct.

counter_evidence.detail: get_api_token_path() constructs the path as /{parts[1]}/{parts[2]}/.api_token. On Hostinger, __DIR__ resolves to something like /home/username/public_html/wp-content/plugins/hostinger-reach/src/Api, yielding /home/username/.api_token — a home-directory path above the webroot that is not HTTP-accessible.

get_order_id() reads the .api_token file server-side only; its value is never reflected into any REST response, localized JavaScript, HTML template, or AJAX response visible to an unauthenticated caller within this plugin's source.

Utils::getApiToken() (vendor copy, same path logic) is also server-side only. No call site in this plugin passes its return value to a public-facing output. Reviewed all public REST handlers and AJAX callbacks — none return or log the .api_token value.

missing_evidence: Confirmation that /.api_token (i.e. /home/{username}/.api_token on Hostinger hosting) is web-accessible or reflected by any other Hostinger-bundled plugin installed on the same server.

Confirmation of the exact filesystem path produced by get_api_token_path() on a real Hostinger deployment — specifically whether parts[2] is 'public_html' (yielding /home/public_html/.api_token, still not web-accessible) or a username.
Evidence of any server misconfiguration or nginx/apache alias that makes the home-directory .api_token file fetchable over HTTP.
Review of other Hostinger-bundled plugins (e.g., hostinger-wp, hostinger-easy-onboarding) to determine whether any public endpoint returns Utils::getApiToken() output.
dynamic_test_plan: Step 1: On a fresh Hostinger hosting account, install and activate the plugin. Note the WordPress installation path (e.g. /home/u123456789/domains/example.com/public_html).

Step 2: Determine get_api_token_path() output: SSH in and run: php -r "$d='/home/u123456789/domains/example.com/public_html/wp-content/plugins/hostinger-reach/src/Api'; $p=explode('/',$d); echo '/'.$p[1].'/'.$p[2].'/.api_token';"
Step 3: Check whether the resulting path (expected: /home/u123456789/.api_token) exists and contains a token value.
Step 4: Attempt to fetch the file directly via HTTP: curl -s https://example.com/.api_token — expect 404 or empty (path is above webroot).
Step 5: Search all other active Hostinger plugins for call sites of Utils::getApiToken() or equivalent that return its value in a public HTTP response.

Step 6: If the token value is obtainable (via any channel), send: POST /wp-json/hostinger-reach/v1/token with body {"csrf_field":"<token_value>","token":"attacker-reach-api-key"} and verify that get_option('hostinger_reach_api_key') is updated with the attacker-supplied value.
Step 7: After successful rebind, confirm that subsequent authenticated admin operations (e.g. GET /wp-json/hostinger-reach/v1/overview) use the attacker's Reach account credentials.
